Attempt Made
To Check Up
On Abranovich

Self-Confessed Member
Of Assassination Gang
Still Held In Settlement

Police Inclined To Theory

Although local French consular
authorities were known to be in
communication with Marseilles
police in an effort to check the
movements of Michael Abranovich,
self-asserted member of the ter-
rorist gang responsible for the
murder of King Alexander I of
Yugoslavia and Joseph Barthou,
former French foreign minister, in
Marseilles last October 9, they
would make no comment yesterday
regarding the progress made.
Abranovich is being detained by
the SMC at the request of French
authorities pending the outcome of
their investigation. He being held
at the Amoy Road Jail.
The man was sentenced in the
First District Court here for assault
on May 20. However, after his con-
viction, two former associates made
charges to Settlement police that
the man had boasted of his rela-
tion to the plotters of the double
murder last October. French au-
thorities were immediately apprais-
ed of the allegation and asked that
the man be held for investigation.
Since his detention for investiga-
tion he has denied any complicity
in the crime and has demanded
the presentation of evidence against
him. However, Judge Sung, before
whom the detention order was pre-
sented, ordered the man held with-
out obliging the French authorities
to present further evidence.
Settlement police were yesterday
inclined to believe that the man
had victimized himself while in the
throes of an alcoholic delirium of
grandeur. He has other egomanical
inclinations, they say, and his loud
boasting of assistance in the re-
gicide is but one of many favorite
usages of the perpendicular pro-
noun with profound imaginative
variance.
French authorities declined to
comment on the length of time it
would take them to complete their
investigation.

尽管众所周知，当地法国领事当局正与马赛警方联系，以核查迈克尔·阿布拉诺维奇（Michael Abranovich）的行踪，此人自称是去年10月9日在马赛谋杀南斯拉夫国王亚历山大一世和前法国外交部长约瑟夫·巴尔杜（Joseph Barthou）的恐怖主义团伙成员，但他们昨日对调查进展不予置评。阿布拉诺维奇应法国当局的要求，由上海公共租界工部局（SMC）拘留，等待调查结果。他被关押在厦门路监狱。
此人曾于5月20日在此间第一特区法院因袭击罪被判刑。然而，在他定罪后，两名前同伙向租界警方指控，此人曾吹嘘自己与去年10月的双重谋杀案策划者有关联。法国当局立即获悉这一指控，并要求拘留此人以进行调查。自被拘留调查以来，他否认参与该罪行，并要求出示针对他的证据。然而，负责审理拘留令申请的宋法官（Judge Sung）下令拘留此人，而未要求法国当局提供更多证据。
租界警方昨日倾向于相信，此人在酒精引起的夸大妄想症发作期间自我受害。警方称，他还有其他自我中心倾向，他大声吹嘘协助弑君只是他频繁使用第一人称代词且伴有丰富想象力的众多习惯之一。
法国当局拒绝对完成调查所需的时间发表评论。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, MAY 24, 1935
10631

Assassin Of
Jugoslav King
Sought Here

Settlement Police Told
Man In Amoy Road Jail
Implicated In Double
Murder At Marseilles

French Seek Extradition
Of Sailor; Evidence
Against Man Is Slight

The eyes of the world were turned on Shanghai yesterday. Today too for that matter. Settlement police had arrested a man who is believed to have been guilty of complicity in the murder last October 9 of King Alexander I of Yugoslavia and Joseph Barthou, former French Foreign Minister.

Michael Abranovich, self-asserted member of the band of terrorists responsible for the regicide, is in the Amoy Road Jail awaiting extradition proceedings which are understood to be in preparation by the French authorities.

A veritable wave of rumor and consternation was raised in Settlement police quarters yesterday when the man appeared in the First Special District Court on a writ of detention sought by the Shanghai Municipal Police. His detention was asked on the grounds that he "was a party to the murder of King Alexander I of Yugoslavia and M. Joseph Barthou, the then French foreign minister, on October 9, 1934, at Marseilles, France."

The official information coming to Settlement officers before the hearing yesterday did not specify any particular crime. It stated that Abranovich was wanted for complicity in murder which was committed in Marseilles in October of last year.

Police Have Little Evidence

Although Settlement police and French consular authorities stated frankly yesterday that so far they have very little evidence against the man, the investigation is proceeding rapidly and it is generally believed that the suspect will be handed over to the French authorities.

When Abranovich appeared in the First Special District Court yesterday he demanded that concrete evidence be produced against him.

Denies Implications

"I have not been concerned in any murder at Marseilles," he said, "and I ask that evidence substantiating that charge be produced before I am held."

Judge Sung, who heard the application, said:

"This is only a detention order. You are not charged formally with any crime. Therefore, no evidence is forthcoming."

Settlement police, late yesterday, were giving the French authorities very close co-operation but they were inclined to believe that the man had been imbued too long with the ephemeral and altogether too short-lived charms produced by a conglomeration of spirits and delusions of grandeur. He boasted, they say, and boasted too strong.

Investigation of Abranovich by Settlement police revealed that he came to the Far East as a sailor aboard the "Calcutta" which sailed for Japan from Anvers, France, to be scrapped. At Kobe, Abranovich, who carried a German passport, returned with other members of the crew of the "Calcutta" to Shanghai.

Sailors Tell Stories

Two fellow sailors, both Greeks, subsequent to Abranovich's arrest and sentence for assault, went to Settlement police and alleged that Abranovich had been concerned with the killing of King Alexander and Foreign Minister Barthou. It was, however, his own statements upon which they based their allegations.

Settlement police made a perfunctory investigation and, after some consultation with French officials, had the man appear in the First Special District Court yesterday.

It is known that Abranovich is a former resident of Marseilles. But whether or not he was there at the time of the double assassination remains for further investigation.

If Abranovich is bound over and returned to France as an accomplice to the killing of King Alexander and M. Barthou it will give governmental agencies of Central Europe a definite lead in running down groups of terrorists who have been ranging throughout that section in recent year.

Memo Submitted

A memorandum was submitted May 21 by Yugoslavia to the League of Nations, criticizing Hungary's report of January 10, 1935, on the results of investigations into terrorist activities on Hungarian territory, launched by the Budapest government in accordance with the League Council's resolution of December 10, 1934.

The memorandum says that Hungary's note of January 10, instead of being an account of the investigations conducted in virtue of the Council's resolution, was merely a retrospective attack against that resolution.

Yugoslavia further expressed the opinion in its note that the inquiry conducted by Hungary was insufficient as regards the methods used and means of surveillance employed in terrorist camps on Hungarian territory. The Budapest report in particular omitted to state how the Croatian terrorists guilty of King Alexander's and Barthou's assassinations obtained the passports that enabled them to proceed to Marseilles where the outrages were committed.

The French delegation on its part yesterday handed Mr. Anthony Eden, British Lord Privy Seal and Rapporteur on the case, a note pointing out the inexactness of certain information contained in Hungary's report.

The Council's resolution of December 10, 1934, was passed following a discussion on Yugoslavia's demarche involving Hungary's political responsibility for the Marseilles murders.

南斯拉夫国王刺客
在此被搜捕

租界警方获悉
厦门路监狱一名男子
涉嫌参与马赛双重谋杀案

法国寻求引渡一名水手；针对该男子的证据微弱

全世界的目光昨天都投向了上海。事实上今天也是如此。租界警方逮捕了一名男子，据信他参与了去年10月9日谋杀南斯拉夫国王亚历山大一世和前法国外交部长约瑟夫·巴尔杜（Joseph Barthou）的罪行。

迈克尔·阿布拉诺维奇（Michael Abranovich），自称是应对此次弑君事件负责的恐怖团伙成员，目前关押在厦门路监狱，等待据悉法国当局正在准备的引渡程序。

昨天，当该男子因上海公共租界工部局警务处申请的拘留令而出庭第一特区地方法院时，租界警界掀起了一股真正的谣言和惊愕浪潮。要求拘留他的理由是，他“参与了1934年10月9日在法国马赛谋杀南斯拉夫国王亚历山大一世和时任法国外交部长约瑟夫·巴尔杜先生的案件”。

在昨天的听证会之前，到达租界警官手中的官方情报并未指明任何具体罪行。情报称，阿布拉诺维奇因涉嫌参与去年10月在马赛犯下的谋杀案而被通缉。

警方掌握证据甚少

尽管租界警方和法国领事当局昨天坦承，目前他们手中针对该男子的证据非常少，但调查正在迅速进行，人们普遍认为这名嫌疑人将被移交给法国当局。

当阿布拉诺维奇昨天出现在第一特区地方法院时，他要求出示针对他的确凿证据。

否认涉案

他说：“我没有参与马赛的 any 谋杀案，我要求在拘押我之前出示证实这一指控的证据。”

审理此申请的宋法官表示：

“这只是一项拘留令。你并没有被正式指控犯有任何罪行。因此，无需提供证据。”

昨天深夜，租界警方正与法国当局进行非常密切的合作，但他们倾向于认为，此人长期沉溺于由酒精混合和大妄念所产生的短暂且转瞬即逝的魅力之中。他们说，他吹嘘过头了。

租界警方对阿布拉诺维奇的调查显示，他是作为“加尔各答号”（Calcutta）轮船的一名水手来到远东的，该船从法国安特卫普驶往日本报废。在神户，持有德国护照的阿布拉诺维奇与“加尔各答号”的其他船员一起返回上海。

水手们讲述故事

两名同为希腊人的 fellow 水手，在阿布拉诺维奇因袭击罪被捕并判刑后，向租界警方报案，声称阿布拉诺维奇参与了杀害亚历山大国王和巴尔杜外交部长的行动。然而，他们的指控是基于阿布拉诺维奇自己的陈述。

租界警方进行了敷衍的调查，并在与法国官员磋商后，于昨天让该男子出庭第一特区地方法院。

已知阿布拉诺维奇曾是马赛居民。但他是否在双重暗杀发生时身处马赛，仍有待进一步调查。

如果阿布拉诺维奇被作为杀害亚历山大国王和巴尔杜先生从犯的共犯被移交并遣返法国，这将给中欧各国政府机构提供一个明确的线索，以追查近年来在该地区活动的恐怖分子团伙。

提交备忘录

南斯拉夫于5月21日向国际联盟提交了一份备忘录，批评匈牙利关于1935年1月10日报告的调查结果，该报告涉及布达佩斯政府根据1934年12月10日国联理事会决议，对在匈牙利领土上开展的恐怖活动进行的调查。

备忘录称，匈牙利1月10日的照会并非是对根据理事会决议进行的调查情况的说明，而仅仅是对该决议的事后攻击。

南斯拉夫在其照会中进一步表示，匈牙利进行的调查在方法和手段上均显不足，特别是在监视匈牙利境内恐怖分子营地方面。布达佩斯的报告尤其未说明犯下杀害亚历山大国王和巴尔杜罪行的克罗地亚恐怖分子是如何获得使他们能够前往马赛实施暴行的护照的。

法国代表团昨天也向英国掌玺大臣兼本案报告人安东尼·艾登先生递交了一份照会，指出匈牙利报告中某些信息的不准确之处。

1934年12月10日的理事会决议是在讨论南斯拉夫就马赛谋杀案追究匈牙利政治责任的外交交涉之后通过的。

er" case loomed in Shanghai
yesterday as French Consular
authorities petitioned the

法国当局

船员同伴
作出书面证词

昨天，上海又浮现出一宗“神秘外国人”案件，法国领事当局向第一特区地方法院申请羁押一名水手迈克尔·阿勃罗诺维奇（Michael Abronovitch），此人被认为涉嫌参与谋杀南斯拉夫亚历山大国王和法国外交部长路易·巴尔杜（Louis Barthou）先生的马赛暗杀案。据说法国领事法院院长德胡格（D'Hooghe）先生已致电巴黎请示指示，这可能导致将囚犯引渡至法国。

虹口周日晚上的一场斗殴导致

（接上页……）
阿勃罗诺维奇被捕。他周一被判袭击罪名成立，并因无法支付30美元罚款而被送进监狱。三名前船友的陈述导致了昨天与马赛暴行有关的事态发展。

两名希腊人和一名波兰人，即囚犯的前船友，已在法国当局面前作出书面证词，称他们曾与他一同乘坐“加尔各答号”轮船（s.s. Calcut）从安特卫普航行至神户，该船在后者港口被出售报废。船上激烈的争吵和阴谋标志着船员之间的关系，据说这些人都是“难缠的角色”。正是在旅途中，阿勃罗诺维奇吹嘘自己是策划了震惊世界罪行的恐怖组织成员。

在神户被捕

阿勃罗诺维奇声称自己有着坎坷的经历，这一点并非完全虚假，因为当他在一家酒店未付账单时，神户警方介入并将该男子移交给德国领事馆。发现他的护照被篡改并予以扣押。他现在作为一个无国籍人士旅行。甚至没有证据表明他的真名是阿勃罗诺维奇。

据说“加尔各答号”的前船长上周将船员带到上海，并将他们滞留在此。周日在北四川路，阿勃罗诺维奇突然袭击了一名 fellow 船员，一名名叫约瑟夫·塞勒（Joseph Seller）的南斯拉夫人，此前两人在非洲的一个港口发生过纠纷。塞勒遭到严重殴打，阿勃罗诺维奇被虹口警方拘留。

静待事态发展。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, MAY 24, 1935

MARSEILLES CRIME
SUSPECT HERE

Yugoslav Seaman Wanted
for King's Murder

HELD IN SETTLEMENT
FOR ASSAULT

Reported by three shipmates to
have admitted participation in the
assassination of King Alexander of
Yugoslavia and M. Louis Barthou,
the French Foreign Minister, at
Marseilles last October, Michael
Abranovich, a Yugoslav seaman, was
being held by the Settlement Police
yesterday. The man, who is also
known as Michkos, arrived here
recently from Japan, where he had
been paid off as a member of the
crew of the ss. Calcut, a ship sold
to scrappers in Kobe. He was in-
volved in a brawl with a former
shipmate in Hongkew on May 19,
arrested, and fined $30 the following
day, with the alternative of serving
a gaol sentence of fifteen days.

It was while the ss. Calcut was in
an African port, en route from
Antwerp to the Orient, that the seeds
of discord which resulted in the
brawl were sown. Throughout the
rest of the voyage, bad blood existed
between Abranovich and other mem-
bers of the crew, and several quar-
rels took place on board. The matter
finally came to a head on the 19th in
Broadway and Abranovich was ar-
rested for assaulting a former ship-
mate.

Accused by Shipmates

A day or so later, three other ex-
members of the Calcut's crew—two
Greeks and a Pole—communicated
with the French Municipal Police,
accusing Abranovich of having ad-
mitted complicity in the Marseilles
assassinations. Once during the trip,
they said, the Yugoslav sailor, while
under the influence of alcohol,
described himself as a terrorist and
boasted of being a member of the
gang who plotted and brought about
the deaths of King Alexander, and M.
Barthou.

The French Police communicated
this information to the French
Consular Court and the statements of
the three sailors were taken down
before M. d'Hooghe, the Presiding
Judge. The French Court then
applied to the Settlement authorities
for the handing over of Abranovich
for questioning.

Writ of Detention

Yesterday, on the application of
the Shanghai Municipal Police, the
First Special District Court issued a
writ of detention against Abranovich
as suspected of having participated
in the Marseilles murders. The
prisoner, questioned by the Chinese
judge, however, denied having taken
part in the assassinations.

The arrest of Abranovich, last
Sunday afternoon, was made on the
complaint of Zeller, a German sea-
man, who alleged that, while he and
a friend were walking along Broad-
way at 6.40 p.m. that day, Abranovich,
with another foreigner who was
armed with a knife, came from be-
hind and attacked him, and, as a
result, he was injured in the head.
Before the Chinese court last Mon-
day, Abranovich was found guilty
and fined $30, with the alternative
of serving a detention term at the
rate of $2 a day.

It was revealed yesterday that al-
though Abranovich claims Yugoslav
nationality, he was born in Russia
and is a naturalised Yugoslav sub-
ject. He is described as being 5 ft.
7 ins. in height, with dark hair and
eyes, and a dark complexion.

马赛罪行
嫌疑人在此

南斯拉夫水手因
谋杀国王被通缉

因袭击罪
被拘于租界

据三名船友报告，承认参与去年10月在马赛刺杀南斯拉夫亚历山大国王和法国外交部长路易·巴尔杜先生，南斯拉夫水手迈克尔·阿布拉诺维奇昨天被租界警方拘留。此人也被称为米奇科斯（Michkos），最近从日本抵达此处，他在那里作为“加尔各答号”轮船（ss. Calcut）的船员被解雇，该船在神户卖给拆船商。5月19日，他在虹口与前船友发生斗殴，被捕，并于次日被罚款30美元，否则需服刑十五天。

当“加尔各答号”轮船在从安特卫普前往东方的途中停靠非洲港口时，导致这场斗殴的不和种子便已播下。在随后的航程中，阿布拉诺维奇与其他船员之间一直存在嫌隙，船上发生了几次争吵。此事最终在19日于百老汇路（今大名路）爆发，阿布拉诺维奇因袭击一名前船友而被捕。

受船友指控

一天左右后，另外三名“加尔各答号”前船员——两名希腊人和一名波兰人——联系了法国市警察局，指控阿布拉诺维奇承认参与马赛暗杀案。他们说，在旅途中有一次，这名南斯拉夫水手在酒精影响下，自称是恐怖分子，并吹嘘自己是策划并导致亚历山大国王和巴尔杜先生死亡的团伙成员。

法国警方将此信息通报给法国领事法院，这三名水手的陈述在庭长德胡格（d'Hooghe）先生面前被记录下来。随后，法国法院向租界当局申请移交阿布拉诺维奇以供讯问。

拘留令

昨天，应上海公共租界工部局警务处的申请，第一特区地方法院对阿布拉诺维奇签发拘留令，怀疑其参与马赛谋杀案。然而，在接受中国法官讯问时，该囚犯否认参与暗杀行动。

阿布拉诺维奇于上周日下午被捕，是基于一名德国水手泽勒（Zeller）的投诉，泽勒指控称，当天下午6点40分，当他和一位朋友沿百老汇路行走时，阿布拉诺维奇与另一名持刀的外国人从背后袭击了他，导致他头部受伤。上周一在中国法庭前，阿布拉诺维奇被判有罪，罚款30美元，否则按每天2美元的标准服拘留刑。

昨天透露，尽管阿布拉诺维奇声称拥有南斯拉夫国籍，但他出生于俄罗斯，是归化的南斯拉夫臣民。据描述，他身高5英尺7英寸，黑发黑眼，肤色黝黑。

CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No.1716.                                          SHANGHAI,      15 May  1935.

Sir,

    I have the honour to inform you that on the 14th of this
month a person presented himself at this Consulate-General with
a Netherlands passport, issued at San Sebastian on 1 June 1934,
No.143718, in the name of Hassein BENJARULAH, born at Malay (Malang ?
12 March 1904 of Netherlands nationality. He stated that his
father was a Javanese and his mother of Spanish descent, but that
he had lived most of the time in the Levan. so that he could not
speak the Netherlands language, being on the other hand well versed
in Arabic and Spanish. He spoke to me in pidgin English and related
how he signed on as a fireman o/b the British s.s. "Calcut", when
this vessel was bunkering at Sabang on 7 April 1934. He showed me
furthermore a certificate of discharge, No.39, dated Osaka 8 May
1935, on which the particulars concerning his "Report of Character"
had been erased and when pressed to explain how this had happened,
he stated that he had incurred the displeasure of the captain, a
Greek, who had smuggled on board three Russian communists, who had
come from Beyruth and had paid the captain the sum of Frs.20.000.-
in order to have them secretly landed in the Netherlands Indies.
Benjarulah stated that during the night, when the vessel was in
Sabang, these persons were stealthily lowered down from the ship
and must have made their way to Sumatra and Singapore. The captain
had threatened him with a pistol, should be dare to divulge this
matter. On arrival in Osaka however Benjarulah states to have
telephoned about it to the Netherlands Consulate at Kobe and then,
when the whole crew had to be discharged, the vessel being sold,
the captain out of revenge is stated to have reported unfavorably
on his conduct. Benjarulah considered that the certificate he had
received from the captain was of no value whatsoever and started
to tear it up, leaving the remnants, which are still in my posses-
sion, on the counter.

    From entries in his passport it appears that this person ob-
tained financial assistance from the Netherlands Consulate at
Marseilles (Frs.111.-) on 26 September 1934 and from the Consulate-
General at Paris (Frs.100.-) on 28 September 1934, for repatriation
home. In Port Said he was given by the Netherlands Consul on 28
January 1935 the sum of £ 10.- to pay his passage to the Netherlands
Indies, whereas from a further note it would appear that he left
Singapore on 28 March 1935 by "Talbout" for Sabang.

    He arrived in Shanghai, coming from Japan, on the 13th of May,
having been paid, he said, £ 2.-.- in Osaka. He was staying in the
Hanbury Institute and requested assistance as he stated to be
penniless.

    He is a short, stoutly built person, wearing European clothes
and a grey cap. He wears a silver ring at his right hand, with the
letters C.C.C. on a red, two trees on a blue and a level (?) on a
white background.

    I should be much obliged to you if you could inform me in case
this person should come to your notice.

                                            I have the honour to be,
                                                        Sir,
                                            Your obedient servant,
                                            [Signature]
                                            Chinese Secretary.

T.P.Givens,Esquire,
Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch),
Shanghai Municipal Police,

SHANGHAI.

    谨此奉告，本月14日，一人持荷兰护照来到本总领事馆。该护照于1934年6月1日在圣塞巴斯蒂安签发，号码为143718，姓名为Hassein BENJARULAH，生于马来亚（Malang？音译：马朗），1904年3月12日出生，荷兰国籍。他声称其父为爪哇人，其母有西班牙血统，但他大部分时间生活在黎凡特地区，因此不会说荷兰语，而精通阿拉伯语和西班牙语。他用洋泾浜英语与我交谈，并讲述了他如何于1934年4月7日英国轮船“Calcut”号（音译：加尔各答号）在沙璜加煤时，在该船签约担任司炉工。此外，他还向我出示了一份解职证书，编号39，日期为1935年5月8日大阪，其中关于其“品行报告”的细节已被擦除。当被追问此事原委时，他称自己惹怒了船长（一名希腊人），该船长走私了三名来自贝鲁特的俄国共产主义者上船，这些人支付了20,000法郎给船长，以便将他们秘密登陆荷属东印度群岛。Benjarulah称，夜间船只停在沙璜时，这些人被偷偷从船上放下，想必已前往苏门答腊和新加坡。船长曾用手枪威胁他，若敢泄露此事便不客气。然而，抵达大阪后，Benjarulah称他曾就此事致电神户的荷兰领事馆，随后因船只出售，全体船员必须解职，船长出于报复，据称对他的行为作了不利报告。Benjarulah认为船长发给他的证书毫无价值，便开始将其撕碎，将残留部分留在柜台上，现仍由我保管。

    从其护照上的记录来看，此人曾于1934年9月26日从马赛荷兰领事馆获得111法郎的资助，并于1934年9月28日从巴黎总领事馆获得100法郎的资助，用于遣返回国。1935年1月28日，荷兰驻塞得港领事给予他10英镑，以支付前往荷属东印度群岛的船费，而根据另一条备注显示，他于1935年3月28日乘“Talbout”号（音译：塔尔博特号）离开新加坡前往沙璜。

    他于5月13日从日本抵达上海，据称在大阪获得了2英镑。他住在汉伯里学会（Hanbury Institute），并请求援助，自称身无分文。

    他身材矮小，体格粗壮，穿着欧式服装，戴着灰色帽子。右手戴着一枚银戒指，戒面上有红色背景上的字母C.C.C.，蓝色背景上的两棵树，以及白色背景上的一个水平仪（？）图案。

Whilst the 2nd accused - Benjarullah Hassein - was being questioned at this Station on the 20/5/35, information was received from some of his ex-shipmates to the effect that a silver finger ring, which he was wearing had been stolen from a passenger aboard the S.S. "Shanghai Maru" during the trip from Japan to Shanghai.

Questioned about the ring, Hassein stated that he obtained it from a boatman vendor of curios in Kobe.

Enquiries from the Chief Steward of the "Shanghai Maru" proved that a passenger named Mr. Paul Reidel, age 16 years, American, student of the China Concordia Seminary Hankow, had reported the loss of a silver ring which was taken from a wash-basin in the ship's lavatory on the 12/5/35, when the ship was passing Woosung, but the Steward was unable to give a description of the missing ring.

The ring found on Hassein is a heavy silver article with an enamel and silver shield in the centre bearing the silver letters "C C C" set in red enamel on top of the shield, a silver theodolite set in white enamel on the left bottom half, and two silver pine trees set in blue enamel on the right bottom half, whilst the whole of the shield is surrounded with two eagles holding flags.

Enquiries by the undersigned and C.D.S. 320.

At about 6.40 p.m. 19/5/35 the complt. late
assistant steward of the s/s Calcut, now in the hands
of shipbreakers in Japan, and his friend one Mr.
Karpovies were walking on the Broadway near Yuenchang
Road when they met the two described on Page No. 1.
who were former shipmates of theirs. The two assaulted
the complt. the 1st. described with his hands, the 2nd.
with a knife. The two then ran away and on the complt.
reporting the affair he was sent to the General Hospi-
tal where after examination the following chit was
issued:-

"Lacerated wound of the scalp, abrasions
and contusions of the face."

The complt. states that when on the voyage from
Europe to the Far East, at a port in Africa he quarrel-
led with the wireless operator of the ship, and after
this quarrel several of the crew took sides with the
disputants. Although the affair has more or less
been settled he believes that the assault on him on
the Broadway was the outcome of this African affair.

Complt. did not know where the accused lived but
believed that they might be found at the Hanbury
Institute, Broadway. This address was visited, the
men were not present but instructions were left with
the staff that should the accused return they should
be detained.
